solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Check through newspaper reports — of Cinderella?

parts.note: a rag is slang for a low-grade newspaper

indicators.note: the abbreviation for check is placed so that it runs through the middle of the word for reports

parts.note: stories are news reports
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone scans tabloid stories hoping for news of Cinderella.
explanation.walkthrough: 'through' sets the chess abbreviation inside the word for reports. The definition is adjectival: Cinderella's is the classic tale of going from poverty to wealth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella's tale is the archetypal story of a pauper rising to great wealth and a royal marriage.

clue.text: Full pelt, running through endless grass

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go through the middle of the shortened grass
the final letter of the word for grass is cut off

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: running signals that the letters of pelt are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: An animal at full pelt races across a field of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final D of the grass word; 'running' scrambles pelt into PLET, which 'through' puts in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Replete is a synonym of full, especially having eaten one's fill.

clue.text: Slowly develop, say, upset condition

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the letters are turned upside down, read from the bottom

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means when introducing an instance
a state is a condition, as in a state of disrepair

explanation.surface: A worrying condition is said to develop slowly and upset the patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the abbreviation for 'for example' upside down, as suits a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To gestate an idea is to let it mature gradually in the mind, as a foetus grows in the womb.

clue.text: Her target, man to abuse?

definitions.note: the definition is a pronoun standing for a woman, of whom the whole clue is a description

indicators.note: abuse here means mistreat or mangle, so the letters of the two words are scrambled

explanation.surface: A woman's target is a man she means to abuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the answer: a shrewish woman whose target is a man to berate. 'to abuse' rearranges TARGETMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A termagant is a violent, scolding woman, so the female pronoun stands for her, with the rest of the clue painting the picture.

clue.text: Sacred object in half of Islam, say? Christianity, primarily

indicators.note: only the front half of the word for a faith is kept

parts.note: Islam is an example of a religion

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so all of Christianity after its opening letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A holy object belongs to half of Islam, or perhaps mainly to Christianity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps RELI from RELIGION; 'primarily' gives C.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is a holy item, such as a saint's bone, venerated by the faithful.

clue.text: Inside vehicle, tie mutilated animal

indicators.note: inside says the word for tie goes within the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to rope something is to tie it

explanation.surface: An animal tied up inside a vehicle has been mutilated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mutilated' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition: a crop-ear is an animal whose ears have been cropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop-ear is a beast, such as a dog or horse, whose ears have been cut short, an old form of mutilation.

clue.text: Run through ceremony in each country

indicators.note: in places the combined letters within the abbreviation for each
the run letter goes through the middle of the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Each country holds a run-through of some ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run through' reads as a phrase meaning rehearse, but it splits: R goes through the ceremony word, making RITRE, which 'in' places inside the abbreviation for each.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is an African nation on the Red Sea coast, north of Ethiopia.

clue.text: A fragile construction, so UFO crashed on the rocks

indicators.note: something on the rocks is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A flimsy craft, so a UFO crashed and was wrecked on rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'on the rocks' rearranges SOUFOCRASHED.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack of playing cards propped up together is the image for any precarious scheme that easily collapses.

clue.text: One resisting work has a problem

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a musical work
a poser is a puzzling problem

explanation.surface: A resister at work runs into a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who opposes a plan is a person resisting it, an objector.

clue.text: Like a Pope's pedigree, covering a long time

indicators.note: the pedigree word is wrapped around the long period

parts.note: a line is a lineage or pedigree
an eon is an age, a very long time

explanation.surface: A papal pedigree stretches back over a vast period.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective relates to Pope Leo; it more commonly means lion-like.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to one of the popes named Leo, such as the Leonine City in Rome walled by Leo IV.

clue.text: Norman's successor Henry is generally eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of electrical inductance

explanation.surface: The successor to a Norman king, Henry, is generally thought odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norman' suggests a monarch, but this is architecture: the Gothic style followed Norman (Romanesque) building in England. 'eccentric' rearranges ISGENERALLY into EARLYENGLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: In English architectural history the Gothic style of about 1180 to 1250 followed the Norman, Romanesque, period.

clue.text: Bohemian needing some pictures met an artist

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bohemian type requires a few pictures after meeting a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Bohemian needing' as the definition, but 'needing' only links the definition to the wordplay; the composer is defined by 'Bohemian' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana, composer of Má vlast, was born in Bohemia, now part of the Czech Republic.

clue.text: Function of bank not so obscure

definitions.meaning: a clearing bank processes cheques, acting as one that settles payments between banks

explanation.surface: A bank's role is said to be less murky than it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearing bank clears cheques, and the comparative of transparent or lucid is more plain.

clue.text: With a huge pot and medals at end of race

parts.note: OBEs are British honours, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, awarded as medals

indicators.note: only the final letter of race is used

explanation.surface: A pot-bellied runner collects medals at the end of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pot' is a belly, not a trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge pot is a large paunch, so someone with one is extremely overweight.

clue.text: The Devil not good in graveyards, dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters are set in motion and land in a new order
not says the letter for good is left out of the word graveyards

explanation.surface: The Devil, hardly benign, dances in churchyards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GRAVEYARDS, leaving RAVEYARDS; 'dancing' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is called the Adversary, a translation of the Hebrew name meaning opponent.

clue.text: Regularly mean with money contributed to farewell card

indicators.note: the pieces are added into the middle of the farewell word

parts.note: vale is Latin for farewell

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of mean

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A miser chips in money to a leaving card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of mean; 'mean' looks like the miser of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a greetings card sent to a sweetheart on 14 February.

clue.text: Mother holds hand at length after firm pledge

indicators.note: after says the mother and length pieces follow the firm

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: the mother word holds the hand word inside it

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
mitt is slang for a hand

explanation.surface: A mother holds a child's hand at length after a firm promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' puts the hand inside the mother, giving MMITTA, and 'after' sets that and L behind the firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Committal is a pledging or commitment, as in the committal of oneself to a course.

clue.text: Presumably not "stick" of furniture?

parts.note: a stick of furniture is a single piece; read literally, a piece that does not stick in place can be shifted

explanation.surface: A query whether an item of furniture is called a stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick of furniture' is an idiom for one item; the clue pretends a stick is something fixed, so furniture that does not stick can be carried around.
explanation.definitionFit: Furniture is movable property, the kind that can be shifted, as opposed to fixtures stuck in place.

clue.text: Holding volume, in Irish, upside down

indicators.note: the in-plus-Irish pieces hold the volume letter between them

parts.note: Erse is the Gaelic language of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone holds a book upside down, in Irish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here but a piece itself; 'Holding' puts the volume letter between it and the Irish language.
explanation.definitionFit: Inverse means turned over or in the opposite order, so upside down.

clue.text: Chief with new bird

parts.note: a capo is a Mafia chief

explanation.surface: A leader arrives with a newly acquired bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a kind of fowl.

clue.text: Facing down, put in large cover

indicators.note: the large letter is inserted into the intimidating word

parts.note: cowing is intimidating, facing someone down

explanation.surface: An instruction to lay a big cover face down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put in' sets L inside COWING.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowling is a removable metal casing over an engine, a kind of hood.

clue.text: Quietly take exception to what one's given

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to resent something is to take exception to it

explanation.surface: A recipient quietly objects to the gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A present is a gift, what someone receives.

clue.text: Vicar, one ladies turned to for dramatic entertainment: that's not new

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: turned means the word for the toilet is read backwards

parts.note: a lav, lavatory, is a ladies

explanation.surface: A vicar, a lone figure the ladies turn to for theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives VAL from LAV. 'ladies' is a British term for a women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival is a fresh production of an older play, so a theatrical show that is not new.

clue.text: Inclined to have answer in forty days

indicators.note: in places the answer letter within the fasting period

parts.note: Lent is the forty-day period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone is minded to find an answer within forty days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A inside LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, so having inclined or tilted.

clue.text: A fresh set of hands making US policy

definitions.meaning: in cards, a redistribution after a misdeal gives every player a fresh hand
Roosevelt's 1930s programme of economic recovery in America

explanation.surface: New workers are brought in to shape American policy.
explanation.definitionFit: In card games a redeal gives new hands; Franklin Roosevelt's Depression-era reforms bore the same name.

clue.text: Place of exile is backed by head of secret police

indicators.note: backed means the word is is written in reverse

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's NKVD, the Soviet secret police

explanation.surface: A place of banishment is supported by a secret-police chief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns IS into SI. 'head of' looks like a first-letter signal, but BERIA is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsarist and Soviet Russia sent prisoners and dissidents to the remote region east of the Urals.

clue.text: Stiff manner is singular, taking in sort of film

indicators.note: the is-plus-singular letters take the film word into their middle

parts.note: cine film is the kind used in old home-movie cameras
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A stiff demeanour is unique, absorbing a certain kind of film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' puts CINE between I and SS.
explanation.definitionFit: Iciness is a frosty coldness of manner, an unwelcoming stiffness.

clue.text: Former spinner almost scores four

definitions.meaning: a gramophone record that turned at 78 revolutions per minute, superseded by LPs
four scores make eighty, and this number falls just short

explanation.surface: An old bowler nearly takes four wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' and 'scores' suggest cricket, a spin bowler and runs; in fact the old shellac disc spun on a turntable, and a score is twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellac discs played at 78 rpm were named by that speed; the number is two short of four twenties.
